patches.value: For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

For every smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and nonnegative integer n, let t_n=n*tau and let q=S_(t_n)f. With the displayed Li-Wu maps F_tau,H_tau, its algebraic step identity is S_(-t_n-tau)[S_tau q+F_tau(q)+H_tau(q)]=f+Stage_(n,tau)(t_n+tau;f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Stage_(n,tau)(s;f))ds-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). The R2 has exactly the Fourier phase covariance, sign and coefficient of D012, including zero output.

For every smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and nonnegative integer n, let t_n=n*tau and let q=S_(t_n)f. With the displayed Li-Wu maps F_tau,H_tau, its algebraic step identity is S_(-t_n-tau)[S_tau q+F_tau(q)+H_tau(q)]=f+Stage_(n,tau)(t_n+tau;f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Stage_(n,tau)(s;f))ds-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). The R2 has exactly the Fourier phase covariance, sign and coefficient of D012, including zero output.

For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution u of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x, obtained by smooth approximation, and sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions on [0,T]. For two real mean-zero L2 data q,r of norms summing to at most B0, the exact solutions satisfy sup_[0,T]||u_q-u_r||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-r||_2. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves all Sobolev norms and for smooth data v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Consequently M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the datum ball.
